lines.text: Here's a square. How big a triangle can you fit inside it?
lines.caption: Here's a square. How big a triangle can you fit inside it?

lines.text: Most kids set it flat on the bottom. <short pause> But that's NOT the biggest one!
lines.caption: Most kids set it flat on the bottom. But that's NOT the biggest one!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out how to fit a bigger one.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out how to fit a bigger one.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: We have a square with side length one.
lines.caption: We have a square with side length one.

lines.text: What is the area of the largest equilateral triangle that fits inside it?
lines.caption: What is the area of the largest equilateral triangle that fits inside it?

lines.text: Equilateral means all three sides are equal.
lines.caption: Equilateral means all three sides are equal.

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what are we really looking for?
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for?

lines.text: Three equal sides, and every corner must stay inside the square.
lines.caption: Three equal sides, and every corner must stay inside the square.

lines.text: The easy one sits flat, with side one. Its area is root three over four.
lines.caption: The easy one sits flat, with side one. Its area is root three over four.

lines.text: That's about forty-three percent of the square.
lines.caption: That's about forty-three percent of the square.

lines.text: But look at all this empty space above it. Can we use it?
lines.caption: But look at all this empty space above it. Can we use it?

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: turn it in a corner

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's our plan: push the triangle into a corner, and turn it.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's our plan: push the triangle into a corner, and turn it.

lines.text: Keep this corner pinned. As it turns, let it grow as big as it can.
lines.caption: Keep this corner pinned. As it turns, let it grow as big as it can.

lines.text: Keep your eye on the side length.
lines.caption: Keep your eye on the side length.

lines.text: It grows, and grows, and then it starts to shrink again.
lines.caption: It grows, and grows, and then it starts to shrink again.

lines.text: The biggest one is right in the middle, at fifteen degrees.
lines.caption: The biggest one is right in the middle, at fifteen degrees.

lines.text: It's perfectly balanced across the diagonal. Its two far corners touch two sides.
lines.caption: It's perfectly balanced across the diagonal. Its two far corners touch two sides.

lines.text: Now let's find its exact size.
lines.caption: Now let's find its exact size.

lines.text: Call this little gap on the right side x.
lines.caption: Call this little gap on the right side x.

lines.text: It's balanced, so the gap along the top is x too.
lines.caption: It's balanced, so the gap along the top is x too.

lines.text: This side is the long side of a right triangle, with legs one and x.
lines.caption: This side is the long side of a right triangle, with legs one and x.

lines.text: So by Pythagoras, its square is one plus x squared.
lines.caption: So by Pythagoras, its square is one plus x squared.

lines.text: The third side cuts off the top right corner. Both legs there are one minus x.
lines.caption: The third side cuts off the top right corner. Both legs there are one minus x.

lines.text: So its square is two times one minus x, all squared.
lines.caption: So its square is two times one minus x, all squared.

lines.text: All three sides are equal, so these two must match!
lines.caption: All three sides are equal, so these two must match!

lines.text: Let's tidy up. Expand the right side, and move everything over.
lines.caption: Let's tidy up. Expand the right side, and move everything over.

lines.text: We get x squared, minus four x, plus one, equals zero.
lines.caption: We get x squared, minus four x, plus one, equals zero.

lines.text: Here's a neat trick. Add three to both sides, and the left is a perfect square!
lines.caption: Here's a neat trick. Add three to both sides, and the left is a perfect square!

lines.text: So x minus two, all squared, equals three.
lines.caption: So x minus two, all squared, equals three.

lines.text: That means x is two plus root three, or two minus root three.
lines.caption: That means x is two plus root three, or two minus root three.

lines.text: Two plus root three is bigger than the whole square. So x is two minus root three.
lines.caption: Two plus root three is bigger than the whole square. So x is two minus root three.

lines.text: Now for the area. The side squared is one plus x squared.
lines.caption: Now for the area. The side squared is one plus x squared.

lines.text: Put in x, and it works out to eight minus four root three.
lines.caption: Put in x, and it works out to eight minus four root three.

lines.text: An equilateral triangle's area is root three over four, times the side squared.
lines.caption: An equilateral triangle's area is root three over four, times the side squared.

lines.text: Careful here: root three times root three is three.
lines.caption: Careful here: root three times root three is three.

lines.text: So the area is two root three, minus three!
lines.caption: So the area is two root three, minus three!

lines.text: That's about forty-six percent of the square. Bigger than forty-three!
lines.caption: That's about forty-six percent of the square. Bigger than forty-three!

lines.text: Here's a second way to finish, without the equilateral area formula.
lines.caption: Here's a second way to finish, without the equilateral area formula.

lines.text: Start with the whole square. Its area is one.
lines.caption: Start with the whole square. Its area is one.

lines.text: Now cut away the three right triangles around our triangle.
lines.caption: Now cut away the three right triangles around our triangle.

lines.text: The two long ones have legs one and x. Together, their area is x.
lines.caption: The two long ones have legs one and x. Together, their area is x.

lines.text: The corner one has two legs of one minus x.
lines.caption: The corner one has two legs of one minus x.

lines.text: One minus x is root three minus one. Square it, take half, and you get two minus root three.
lines.caption: One minus x is root three minus one. Square it, take half, and you get two minus root three.

lines.text: And x is also two minus root three! So we cut that away twice.
lines.caption: And x is also two minus root three! So we cut that away twice.

lines.text: One, minus two times two minus root three. That's two root three, minus three again!
lines.caption: One, minus two times two minus root three. That's two root three, minus three again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? To double-check, or if you forget the area formula.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? To double-check, or if you forget the area formula.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: A is the flat triangle with side one. It fits, but it's not the biggest.
lines.caption: A is the flat triangle with side one. It fits, but it's not the biggest.

lines.text: B forgets to square the side in the area formula.
lines.caption: B forgets to square the side in the area formula.

lines.text: D is a triangle exactly one unit tall. But then its base is too wide to fit!
lines.caption: D is a triangle exactly one unit tall. But then its base is too wide to fit!

lines.text: Choice E uses the diagonal as a side. That pokes right out of the square!
lines.caption: Choice E uses the diagonal as a side. That pokes right out of the square!

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Always check that your shape really fits.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Always check that your shape really fits.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a bigger square, with side length two.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a bigger square, with side length two.

lines.text: What's the area of the largest equilateral triangle that fits inside it?
lines.caption: What's the area of the largest equilateral triangle that fits inside it?

lines.text: Use the same plan. Pin a corner, and find the gap.
lines.caption: Use the same plan. Pin a corner, and find the gap.

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Call the gap x again.
lines.caption: Let's check. Call the gap x again.

lines.text: One side squared is four plus x squared.
lines.caption: One side squared is four plus x squared.

lines.text: The other is two times two minus x, all squared.
lines.caption: The other is two times two minus x, all squared.

lines.text: Set them equal and tidy up. x minus four, all squared, equals twelve.
lines.caption: Set them equal and tidy up. x minus four, all squared, equals twelve.

lines.text: So x is four minus two root three.
lines.caption: So x is four minus two root three.

lines.text: Now cut the corners. The square's area is four.
lines.caption: Now cut the corners. The square's area is four.

lines.text: The two long triangles add up to eight minus four root three. And the corner one is the same!
lines.caption: The two long triangles add up to eight minus four root three. And the corner one is the same!

lines.text: So the area is four, minus two times that. Eight root three, minus twelve!
lines.caption: So the area is four, minus two times that. Eight root three, minus twelve!

lines.text: Neat check: that's four times our first answer. Double the side, and the area grows four times!
lines.caption: Neat check: that's four times our first answer. Double the side, and the area grows four times!

lines.text: If you found eight root three minus twelve, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found eight root three minus twelve, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: To fit the biggest shape, push it into a corner, and turn it until it's balanced.
lines.caption: To fit the biggest shape, push it into a corner, and turn it until it's balanced.

lines.text: Then let the equal sides give you one equation.
lines.caption: Then let the equal sides give you one equation.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
